t: Ahab/Israel will suffer because of sparing Ben-Hadad
s: Because Ahab released Ben-Hadad, whom God had doomed, a prophet said Ahab's life would go for his. Ahab was later killed fighting the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead.

t: Micaiah predicts Ahab & Jehoshaphat will be defeated
Ahab will die and dogs will lick up his blood
s: After Naboth's murder, Elijah told Ahab that dogs would lick his blood. When Ahab's chariot was washed at the pool of Samaria, the dogs licked up his blood.

t: Syria will return in spring and be defeated in the plain
s: The prophet warned Ahab that Ben-Hadad would come back at the turn of the year, and said that because Syria called the LORD a god of the hills, Israel would win in the plain. At Aphek Israel killed 100,000 Syrians.

t: A lion will kill the man who refused the prophet's word
s: A prophet told a man who refused to strike him at the LORD's word that a lion would kill him on leaving. A lion found him and killed him.

t: Jezebel will be eaten by dogs
s: Elijah said dogs would eat Jezebel at Jezreel. When Jehu took power she was thrown from a window, and only her skull, feet and palms were left to bury.

t: Elijah will be taken to heaven on a certain day
s: The prophets at Bethel and Jericho knew God would take Elijah that day. A chariot of fire parted Elijah and Elisha, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind.

t: Elisha predicts the Moabites will be conquered through a miracle of water
Elisha predicts Naaman will be healed if Naaman obeys him
Every male of Ahab's house to be cut off (after his days)
s: Elijah declared Ahab's dynasty would be wiped out, but after Ahab humbled himself the disaster was put off to his son's days. Jehu killed Joram and all of Ahab's remaining house in Jezreel and Samaria.

t: Blood of Naboth repaid on Ahab's son in Naboth's field
s: Jehu recalled the LORD's oath that Naboth's blood would be repaid in that very plot. He had Joram's body thrown onto Naboth's field.

t: Micaiah: Israel scattered and Ahab will not return in peace
s: Against 400 court prophets, Micaiah foresaw Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd and said Ahab would not come back safely. The army fled and Ahab died of a chance arrow.

t: Elijah predicts Ahaziah I will die because of consulting Baal-Zebub
s: Ahaziah, injured in a fall, sent to ask the god of Ekron whether he would recover. Elijah said he would never leave his bed, and he died.

t: Elijah predicts Elisha will receive a double portion of Elijah's spirit
s: Elijah said Elisha would have his request if he saw Elijah taken. Elisha saw it, parted the Jordan with Elijah's mantle, and the prophets said Elijah's spirit rested on him.

t: A seven-year famine predicted (881-875 BC)
s: Elisha warned the Shunammite woman that God had called for a seven-year famine. She lived in Philistia for seven years and on her return got her land back.

t: Ditches filled with water and Moab defeated
s: Elisha said the dry valley would fill with water without wind or rain, and Moab would be given into the kings' hands. Water came in the morning; the Moabites took it for blood, attacked, and were beaten.

t: Jehoshaphat's ships with Ahaziah will be broken
s: Eliezer told Jehoshaphat that because he partnered with wicked Ahaziah, God would break his ships. The fleet built at Ezion-geber was wrecked before it could sail to Tarshish.

t: Elisha predicts his servant, Gehazi, will become leprous because of greed
The barren Shunammite will hold a son about this time next year
s: Elisha told his childless hostess at Shunem that she would embrace a son at the same season the next year. She conceived and bore a son at the time he named.

t: Naaman will be clean if he washes seven times in the Jordan
s: Elisha told the Syrian commander to wash seven times in the Jordan to be healed of leprosy. He did, and his skin became like a child's.

s: Elisha told Hazael that God had shown him Hazael would be king of Syria. The next day Hazael smothered Ben-Hadad and took the throne.

t: Siege of Samaria: fine flour for a shekel by tomorrow
s: In a starving, besieged Samaria, Elisha said that by the same time next day flour and barley would sell cheaply at the gate. The Syrians fled in the night, and food sold at exactly the prices he named.

t: The doubting officer will see the plenty but not eat of it
s: The king's officer scoffed at Elisha's word, and Elisha said he would see it but not eat of it. He was trampled to death in the gate by the crowd rushing to the food.

t: Gehazi struck with Naaman's leprosy for his greed
s: Gehazi secretly took silver and clothes from Naaman. Elisha said Naaman's leprosy would cling to him and his descendants, and he left white with leprosy.

t: Hazael will do great evil to Israel
s: Elisha wept as he told Hazael the harm he would do to Israel's strongholds and people. In Jehu's and Jehoahaz's days Hazael struck Israel's territory and left Jehoahaz only a tiny army.

t: Elisha predicted Israel will defeat Aram three times

t: Peter says Pentecost fulfills Joel's prophecy
s: God would pour out His Spirit on all kinds of people. Peter said Pentecost was this, and Johnson calls it a partial fulfilment. The cosmic signs are still future.

t: Send away Israel's mercenaries and God will give victory over Edom
s: A man of God told Amaziah not to take Israel's hired troops into battle, saying God could give him more than the money lost. He sent them home and defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt.

t: Amaziah will be killed because of sin
s: A prophet told Amaziah that God had decided to destroy him for worshipping the gods of conquered Edom. Israel defeated him, and conspirators later killed him at Lachish.

t: God will abandon Joash because he killed the prophet Zechariah
s: Zechariah warned that because Judah had forsaken God, God had forsaken them; dying, he asked God to see and require it. A small Syrian force defeated Judah, and Joash was murdered by his servants.

t: The false prophet and the mark of the beast (666)
s: A second beast makes the world worship the first and forces a mark without which no one can buy or sell. Johnson cites Irenaeus on the 666 name.

t: 144,000 sealed from the tribes of Israel
s: Twelve thousand from each tribe are sealed before the judgments. Johnson sees them winning converts in the first half of the Tribulation.

t: The seven seal judgments
s: The seals bring conquest, war, famine and death (a quarter of the earth), martyrs, a great earthquake with the sun darkened, and silence in heaven.

t: The seven trumpet judgments
s: The trumpets strike a third of the land, sea, waters and lights. Then come locusts for five months and an army of 200 million that kills a third of mankind. At the seventh trumpet the kingdoms become Christ's.

t: The seven bowl judgments; the Euphrates dried up
s: The bowls bring sores, the sea and rivers turned to blood, scorching sun and darkness. The sixth dries the Euphrates for the kings of the east, and the seventh brings the greatest earthquake and hundred-pound hail.

t: Mystery Babylon falls in one hour
s: The harlot on the scarlet beast is judged, and the great city's plagues come in one day as merchants mourn.

t: The marriage supper of the Lamb
s: The bride has made herself ready, and those called to the Lamb's marriage supper are blessed. The Biblefacts chart places it with the Second Coming.

t: Tribulation martyrs raised to reign with Christ
s: Those beheaded for refusing the mark live and reign with Christ in the first resurrection. Johnson places this at the Second Coming, when the raptured saints return with Christ.

t: Satan bound in the abyss for a thousand years
s: An angel binds the dragon and seals him in the bottomless pit for a thousand years, so he can deceive the nations no more until they end.

t: The Millennium: Christ reigns 1,000 years (6001–7000 AM)
s: Christ reigns from Jerusalem for a thousand years of peace, when nations no longer learn war. Johnson's calendar starts the Kingdom age at 6001 AM (AD 2076). He sees it in the Feast of Tabernacles and cites Papias, Justin, Irenaeus and Lactantius for a literal millennium.
